children: The FTSE MIB plunged 1.7% to 51,545 on Friday amid broad selling as energy-supply concerns weighed on the index.
Eurozone sovereign yields rebounded after reports that Saudi Arabia would not supply oil to European buyers next month, raising fears of further inflationary pressure.
In Milan, worries over Italy's swelling public debt also weighed, with the latest budget plan projecting debt near 139% of GDP, replacing Greece at the eurozone's bottom.
Higher bond yields pressured bank balance sheets, with Unipol, UniCredit, Banco BPM and BPER Banca all falling more than 2%.
Defense stocks underperformed, led by Fincantieri (-1%).
Utilities reversed recent gains as European gas prices rebounded, led by A2A (-3.2%).
Stellantis plunged 5.2% after reports it plans to sell its Toronto facility, citing "no long-term business case" for auto manufacturing there amid unpredictable US–Canada trade policies.

title: FTSE MIB Drops Sharply on Friday
